name: plate-50-engine-reprint-1c
version_tag: PLACEMENT PATCHED 2026-08-09 — the four detent springs were all centred at x=222, which the gate refused: at 80x19.3mm each they occupied X[182,262] and ran 6mm OFF a 256mm bed, and three of them also bit 12mm into 157_fixture_r63 (X[62,194] Y[26,102]). THE x=222 COLUMN WAS SIZED FOR THE PRE-#162 CANTILEVER SPRINGS; the bridge-type rev held on both ends is 80mm long and no longer fits there. Re-placed: soft and one med lie horizontally in the free band between the fixture (ends y102) and the sun towers (start y140), at [50,121] and [140,121]; the other med and firm are rotated 90deg into the free right-hand column at [225,60] and [225,160], where 80mm of length runs vertically. Resulting tightest gaps: 9mm to the fixture, 9mm to the sun towers, 14mm to the carriers, 10mm between the two horizontal springs; all bodies >=5mm from every edge; tallest part still the 29.5mm fixture. | #152 ENGINE REPRINT, SINGLE COLOUR — fixture r63, three sun tower pieces, both carrier arms. Companion to plate-49; split off so the two-colour parts are not hostage to the 34cm3 fixture. 157_fixture_r63 REPLACES 148_fixture_r62: the key now reaches 29.5 and carries the drive post to 26.0, because at 6.5 pitch the old key stopped short and left the top sun pieces free to rotate, which destroys the #134 clocking. Sun tower piece is now 6.50 tall (band 1.5 + slim core 5.0) — PRINT THREE. The 5.0 is taken in the piece itself and NOT as a stack of 0.5mm shims: a 0.5mm shim prints at 2.5 layers, rounds to 0.4 or 0.6, and that z error walks the mesh lamina off its band. Carrier arms carry the #152 stepped bore (4.00 on the 4.20 spigot) and arm 1's riser steps at 19.2 for arm 2; arm 2's riser does NOT step — nothing stacks on the leap post, so it keeps full section. 147_sun_spacer is byte-identical to what is already printed — DO NOT reprint it. 6 objects, flat, no supports, xy-comp -0.06, seam aligned. | QUIET. | +#156/#157 DETENT, ALL PRINTED (Ron's law: no wire anywhere in the build). 164 star: 31 full-pitch V sawtooth ring under the board, pegs into the board's new underside sockets, V-bottom at 267.10 = 270 - pitch/4. TWO BRIDGES (#157, Ron's idea): 163 south + 166 north holders, 185.81 deg apart = EXACTLY 16 pitches. NOT 180.00: with 31 notches the point opposite a valley is a crest, and two sawtooth detents in perfect anti-phase sum to a FLAT potential - zero centering, double friction. At 16 pitches both noses seat at once, torques add, radial loads cancel to 1%. The quarter-pitch re-clock makes the bearings flip-symmetric, so ONE spring design serves both bridges - flip it over for the north. 165 springs x4 (soft/med/med/firm, leaf 2.6/3.0/3.4): flat 2.0mm plug-in leaves, 5-minute consumable prints, resting strain ~0.1% (creep-negligible; escape ~0.4% is transient). Press the 8.3 tab into the 8.0 pocket, nose in a V, holder butts the plate edge, tape the far end. START WITH THE SOFT PAIR (Ron's bench: removing the mis-phased v16 detent un-jammed the machine - crest resistance is paid from the strike window as wind-up; soft pair ~1.1N at the crest, and the new star's crests are phase-locked to mid-stroke where the arm is strongest). Step up stiffness only if July rejection slips. Gate: no dead zone, restoring slope everywhere below the 5.80 crest, July 4.63 release comes home on both bridges, curves identical north/south to <1um. NOTE plates 49+50 are a matched set: the plate-49 board carries the peg sockets.
